video_title: Why One Domain Model Breaks at Scale
core_insight: Complex domains cannot be captured by a single shared model; DDD uses Bounded Contexts with Ubiquitous Language to let teams own coherent models and translate between them.

scenes.voice: Why does a simple CRUD app turn into a mess as the business grows?
scenes.visual: Split screen: simple form on left, tangled code and database tables on right.

scenes.voice: In banking, insurance, logistics, the code starts mirroring tables, not the business. Developers and business use the same words with different meanings. Rules leak into controllers and services.
scenes.visual: Words Customer, Order floating between Sales and Support teams with different definitions.

scenes.voice: The real constraint is cognitive. You cannot fit a complex domain into one consistent model across a large team.
scenes.visual: Large team around one whiteboard, model explodes into contradictions.

scenes.voice: Reasonable first approach is one unified model. It works for small teams, then breaks. Sales Order and Fulfillment Order need different invariants.
scenes.visual: Single box labeled Order with conflicting rules appearing.

scenes.voice: DDD draws borders. A Bounded Context is a place where one Ubiquitous Language is valid. Inside, the model is rich and behavior-rich. Between borders we translate.
scenes.visual: Territory map with borders around Sales and Fulfillment.

scenes.voice: Sales can have its Order aggregate, Fulfillment its Shipment aggregate. An Anti-Corruption Layer translates events between them so one model doesn't corrupt the other.
scenes.visual: Mermaid diagram showing Business Experts to Ubiquitous Language to two Bounded Contexts with Anti-Corruption Layer.
scenes.mermaid:
graph LR
    Business[Business Experts] --> UL[Ubiquitous Language]
    UL --> BC1[Sales Bounded Context]
    UL --> BC2[Fulfillment Bounded Context]
    BC1 -- Anti-Corruption Layer --> BC2
    BC1 --> Agg1[Aggregate: Order]
    BC2 --> Agg2[Aggregate: Shipment]

scenes.voice: You gain clarity and team autonomy, you pay upfront modeling cost and learning curve. Use DDD when misunderstanding the domain costs more than modeling it.
scenes.visual: Scale balancing modeling cost vs change cost.
scenes.on_screen_text: Trade-off: design time vs change cost

scenes.voice: Model the domain, not the database. Boundaries let you scale language.
scenes.visual: Clean boxes with borders, behavior inside aggregates.

mental_model: Think of the domain as territory. Draw borders where a single coherent language can be maintained. Inside a border, keep a rich behavior model with aggregates protecting invariants. Between borders, translate explicitly.
final_takeaway: One ubiquitous language per bounded context, not one model for the whole business.
